title: Double Adjacent Equal Elements and Shift Zeros

content.problemStatement:
Rearrange the array

Write a program to convert the array in such a way that double its value and replace the next number with 0 if current and next element are same and rearrange the array such that all 0's shifted to the end.



For Example

The given array is: 0 3 3 3 0 0 7 7 0 9

The new array is: 6 3 14 9 0 0 0 0 0 0

Explanation:

   In the given array the second and third element is equal hence hence double the first 3 and make the next index value as 0. The element which which is in third index doesn't have any match so leave as it is. finally move all zero to the end
content.inputFormat: The input contains an integer N which is the size of the array and in the array and in the next line N elements will be there
content.outputFormat: Print the updated array with the space

solution.approach: Multiply adjacent equal elements by 2 and zero out second, then shift all zeros to end.

code.Python3:
import sys
def main():
    toks = sys.stdin.read().split()
    if not toks: return
    n = int(toks[0])
    arr = [int(x) for x in toks[1:n+1]]
    i = 0
    while i < n - 1:
        if arr[i] != 0 and arr[i] == arr[i+1]:
            arr[i] *= 2; arr[i+1] = 0; i += 2
        else: i += 1
    non_zeros = [x for x in arr if x != 0]
    zeros = [0] * (n - len(non_zeros))
    print(" ".join(str(x) for x in (non_zeros + zeros)))
if __name__ == "__main__": main()

solution.editorial: Iterate i from 0 to N-2. If arr[i] == arr[i+1] != 0, double arr[i] and set arr[i+1] = 0. Then move non-zeros forward and zeros to end.
